cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Hand Over the Proof
cards.instruction: Persuade someone to surrender information, evidence, a key, or access that would let you proceed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Hand me the drawer key before I sign the club accounts. Please.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. My signature covers the receipts too. Let me check how it adds up.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: If you find a mistake, my name goes on it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put mine beside yours. Give me the key and we'll correct it together before either name goes outside this room.

mechanism: A directs signing accounts but needs the drawer key, offering shared responsibility and private correction to persuade B to surrender access.
confusable: Unlike merely asking for the total, A seeks actual supporting receipts; borrowed authority bears risk with B instead of commanding access without reassurance.
comparison: Financial accountability and shared signatures differ from privacy over a family note.
seedUse: D132-b key, receipts and shared names; S02-a changes responsibility terms to keep B cooperating.
